recipes.name: FunSearch · original author pilot, timeout v2
setup: Reuse the exact original-author FunSearch checkout and its prepared isolated environment, including the OpenAI SDK and a hashed bubblewrap executable.

The v2 gateway driver fixes the SDK request timeout to 330 seconds, no SDK retries, six generated samples and a 2400-second outer runtime template. It does not change native search, scoring or the gateway service.

profiles.description: Original-author native admissible-set pilot with a 330-second client deadline above the separately configured 300-second gateway deadline.

evaluation.description: Native reconstruction, scoring specification, admission and island database are unchanged; the supplied sandbox executes each reconstructed program in a credential-free network-isolated Linux namespace with a deadline.

argument_help: --model exact gateway ID. --max-samples, if supplied, must be 6. A separately hashed request.executables.bubblewrap is required.
limitations: Transport-only v2 variant; the existing original and reimplementation recipe identities and default 180-second behavior remain intact.
One sampler and evaluator, two native islands, original constant-weight admissible-set specification at (9,5). Six generated samples plus one seed sandbox call; native scores remain noncanonical.
The client uses 330 seconds per SDK operation with max_retries=0. The operator gateway deadline is expected to be 300 seconds and is not changed or independently measured by this driver.

Prepared templates retain the 2400-second whole-process timeout. A caller running this driver directly must supply its own process boundary. A timed-out dispatched generation has unknown outcome/cost, and is never counted as returned or automatically retried.
This is a small integration pilot, not a reproduction of the paper or evidence of improvement.
